records.title: Diaspora as Anticipatory Actors in Conflict-Induced Displacement Consultancy
records.summary: Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence. Purpose of the consultancy Under the project Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement (AHEAD), the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and DEMAC are commissioning a consultancy to consolidate lessons and findings on the role of diaspora in anticipatory action under the project. records.title: Conduct a streamlined audit of pest-related data management across ISABU, DPV and MINEAGRIE to identify priority gaps and overlaps
records.summary: Background Effective pest surveillance, diagnosis, risk assessment, phytosanitary decision-making and pest management depend on the availability of reliable, timely and accessible pest-related data. Such data may include information on pest occurrence and distribution, pest identification and diagnosis, crop and host associations, disease incidence, pest outbreaks, surveillance activities, pest risk assessments, phytosanitary measures and pest management interventions. In Burundi, pest-related information is generated and managed by several institutions, including the Institut des Sciences Agronomiques du Burundi (ISABU) , the Direction de la Protection des Végétaux (DPV) and the Ministère de l'Environnement, de l'Agriculture et de l'Élevage (MINEAGRIE) . These institutions have complementary mandates and may maintain data in different formats, systems and locations. The absence of a consolidated understanding of existing pest-related datasets, data flows, management practices and institutional responsibilities can result in data gaps, duplication, parallel data collection, inconsistent terminology and difficulties in accessing or integrating information. records.summary: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. records.title: Request for Proposal WAZZII Platform Feature Development and Service Design
records.summary: Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology girls choose, use and trust. Across Africa and South Asia, our youth brands — including Wazzii and Tuki in Kenya, Big Sis in South Africa, Chhaa Jaa and Bol Behen in India, and Yegna in Ethiopia — reach millions of adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with content and digital tools that support the decisions shaping their lives, from sexual and reproductive health (SRH) to wellbeing, education and work. Our approach is girl-centred by design: girls co-create our products, our evidence teams measure what actually changes for them, and our safeguarding architecture treats their safety as a design constraint, never an afterthought. Girl Effect has spent a decade building conversational products for young people, and several years deliberately and publicly charting what responsible technology for girls looks like. What is WAZZII Today. WAZZII is Girl Effect’s WhatsApp-based chatbot for AGYW in Kenya, offering confidential SRH information, signposting and human help desk support in English and Sheng.
